newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia wheat harvest enters final stage.
newsitem.headline: Croatia wheat harvest enters final stage.

text.p: Croatia hopes to complete wheat harvesting within a few of days if good weather holds, state news agency Hina said on Tuesday, quoting the Agriculture Ministry.
Wheat has so far been harvested on 176,450 hectares, or 85.5 percent, of the area sown to the country's main cereal, the ministry said.
It put the average yield at over four tonnes per hectare.
The 1997 crop has been forecast at 820,000 tonnes, which would more than meet domestic demand.
But some analysts earlier raised doubts about the government-set target, claiming that wet June weather had damaged wheat and maize crops.

Some 80,000 tonnes of wheat was said to have been harvested in the Serb-held area of Eastern Slavonia, following earlier claims that only 15 percent of the crop had been reaped. The Ministry said most of the crop reached government silos.
Other crops including barley, rye, oats and rapeseed have mostly been harvested, Hina said.
